name: snap7
desc: Ethernet communication suite that works natively with Siemens S7 PLCs
why: Opens a door into Siemens S7 industrial PLC protocols over Ethernet, letting you talk to real factory controllers from your laptop.

brief.what_it_is: Snap7 is a multi-platform Ethernet communication library for talking to Siemens S7 PLCs (industrial controllers) from a PC or small board. Per the SourceForge listing it has three components, Client, Server and Partner, and offers wrappers for C/C++, .NET/Mono, Pascal, LabVIEW and Python. Your program makes calls to read and write PLC data over the network; the PLC side is the real controller on the factory network. It is licensed LGPLv3. The official homepage is a frameset with no readable content, so this description comes from the SourceForge project page.
brief.why_it_exists: It lets ordinary PC software exchange data with Siemens S7 controllers over Ethernet without buying Siemens' own communication software. The SourceForge summary says it is designed to transfer large amounts of high-speed data in industrial facilities.
brief.how_it_works: The library implements the S7 communication protocol over Ethernet in native code, with no third-party dependencies. It offers synchronous and asynchronous data transfer, and both polling and unsolicited flows, where the PLC pushes data when it chooses. Its own description also says it adapts endianness at runtime and needs no compiler switch.
brief.install_notes: No install step is documented in the pages I could read. The SourceForge listing says it needs no installation and no configuration and has no third-party library dependencies. It also says ready-to-run projects and makefiles are included for rebuilding in many platforms without being a C++ expert. Downloads are on SourceForge as snap7-full zip, 7z and tar.gz archives; the search-term list mentions versions 1.4.2 and 2.0.2-x64. I did not find brew-specific instructions, and I saw no commands. Real use needs a Siemens PLC reachable over Ethernet.
brief.standout: It runs on Linux, Windows, Mac, BSD and Solaris, down to small ARM boards such as the Raspberry Pi, with the client and server both in the same library. Its own description says a full working server example is no bigger than a 'Hello world'.
brief.status: Appears maintained, though the evidence is thin. The SourceForge page shows Last Update 2025-06-24, 939 downloads this week, and a 2013 registration date. A recent 2026-dated review also appears on the page. I did not check a git commit history, and no release notes were visible.
brief.caveats: The official homepage is a frameset with no readable content, and the GitHub URL I guessed (SiemensAG/snap7) returned 404. Snap7 is a community project by Davide Nardella rather than an official Siemens product, even though the repo is named SiemensAG in my guess. It talks to live industrial controllers, so mistakes can affect real machinery; test against a simulator or a bench PLC first. The features list includes set/clear password functions for full access to protected PLCs, which is security-sensitive. Supported models per the listing are S7-300/400/1200/1500, WinAC, LOGO 0BA7/0BA8, S7-200 and SINAMICS. Newer or other PLC families may not be covered.
quotes: Very easy to use, a full working server example is not bigger than the “Hello world”.
No dependence on any third-party libraries, no installation needed, zero configuration.
Designed to transfer large amounts of hi-speed data in industrial facilities, it scales easily, down to small Linux Arm boards such as Raspberry PI.

https://github.com/SiemensAG/snap7 - failed, HTTP 404 (guessed URL, not confirmed)
https://sourceforge.net/projects/snap7/ - worked, full project listing with description, features, license, and last update

judge.reason: Snap7 makes Siemens S7 industrial communication tangible: a small program can read and write controller data, or run a server, opening a door into factory protocols.

entry.title: Snap7
entry.tldr: An Ethernet library that speaks the Siemens S7 protocol, so your own code can read and write memory in real factory PLCs, or in a fake one it hosts.
entry.deeper_look:
Snap7 is a native library that implements the S7 communication protocol over Ethernet. Siemens S7 PLCs are the industrial controllers that run assembly lines, pumps and building systems. Your program makes calls to read and write data blocks on the controller, and the library handles the network conversation.

It has three parts: Client, Server and Partner. The Client reads and writes a PLC. The Server pretends to be a PLC, so you can build and test without hardware. Partner is for peer-to-peer exchange, including the mode where the PLC pushes data when it chooses instead of waiting to be polled. Wrappers exist for C/C++, .NET/Mono, Pascal, LabVIEW and Python.

It exists so ordinary PC software can exchange data with S7 controllers without buying Siemens' own communication software. It is a community project by Davide Nardella, not an official Siemens product. The underlying idea is that industrial automation runs on documented-enough network protocols, and once you can speak one, a laptop or a Raspberry Pi becomes a peer of the machinery. The project says a full working server example is "not bigger than the 'Hello world'".

The Homebrew formula installs the library only. It has no executables, so you use it by writing code against it.
entry.install:
brew install snap7
# Installs the library only, with no executables. Talking to a real PLC needs a Siemens S7 controller reachable over Ethernet. The Server component can stand in for one.
entry.whats_unique: Client, Server and Partner live in one dependency-free library, so you can run both ends of an S7 conversation on a laptop. It also scales down to small ARM boards.
entry.caveats: It talks to live industrial controllers, so test against the built-in server or a bench PLC first; the official homepage is an empty frameset, and Homebrew installs no command-line tools.
